facts: F1: Every attempt is already one Notification row the Events log renders with its error
F2: Notification has no flip reference; a delayed retry must persist one through a migration
F3: 'Sending' in-flight marker; only TransportError is handled, other exceptions escape
F4: 200-character error column written untruncated; overflow fails the update on PostgreSQL/MySQL
F5: Channel.notify is the single entry point with four callers; Test!/deletion pass unsaved dummies
F6: No delayed retry exists; the flip is claimed first and a failed attempt is final
F7: No queue or scheduler; the sendalerts poll loop needs durable pending-retry rows
F8: Work is claimed with conditional UPDATEs; a retry claim must follow the pattern
F9: In-attempt retries differ by transport; replace or stack is open (up to 12 HTTP requests)
F10: Typed failures (permanent disables); re-check disabled, deleted and no-op state at retry time
F11: Non-permanent failures waiting cannot fix ('not enabled', 'Email not verified')
F12: SMS/WhatsApp/call quota is spent per attempt even when the provider call fails, never refunded
F13: Monthly-limit refusals email a limit notice to the team on every attempt
F14: Token-bucket rate limits (6 a minute) fail non-permanently and refill within a minute
F15: Signal CAPTCHA failure emails site admins and the owner on every attempt
F16: Incident integrations pair down with recovery; a late down retry re-opens an incident
F17: Group fan-out: member rows, members called even if disabled, 'N out of M' failure
F18: Test-style sends are synchronous, unsaved and outside the check's log
F19: Late failures from Twilio callbacks and bounces update the same row; open whether they retry
F20: Channel last_notify/last_error summarise the latest attempt and drive the UI and call order
F21: Small delivery capacity; retries sharing workers can delay first alerts
F22: Per-attempt operator signals: log lines, statsd counters, dwell time, metrics endpoint
F23: Past notifications are listed only on the check's Events page
F24: Only 'down' notifications are listed; up attempts are an open question
F25: Notifications are hidden behind the unticked 'Downtime alert' filter
F26: Live updates fetch only newly created rows, never changes to existing rows
F27: Live-update script is broken (undefined dateFormat); new rows need a reload
F28: Retention cap, pruning, clear events and cascades delete rows and their retry state
F29: Rows are described from the integration's current settings
F30: Error text is auto-escaped and visible to everyone who can open the check
F31: Webhook form promises retries 'up to 2 additional times'
F32: Alert text is built at send time, so a retry is not identical
F33: ORM on SQLite/PostgreSQL/MySQL/MariaDB; numbered migrations (latest 0123); UTC
F34: Polls use partial indexes; a due-retry query needs its own index
F35: Server-rendered templates with small jQuery scripts; no SPA or build step
F36: Settings are documented environment variables; none controls retries
F37: Code and contribution rules (mypy --strict, ruff, tests, changelog, AI policy)
F38: Existing log test asserts the absence of text the template never renders
F39: Precedent commits show the footprint of similar work
F40: Open: is a pending retry dropped after recovery, pause or a newer flip?
F41: Open: are the 1, 5 and 25 minutes counted from the first failure or from each failure?

worst_misses: F4: a transport error over 200 characters (Opsgenie or Zulip remote text) makes Channel.notify's error UPDATE fail on PostgreSQL/MySQL; P3 writes retry_at in that same UPDATE, so such a failure stays at 'Sending', is never retried, and aborts the flip's remaining integrations.

F27: AD-7 says retry rows appear in the existing live polling as they are written, but the shipped log.js throws on the undefined dateFormat, so attempts arriving 1 to 31 minutes later stay invisible on an open Events page until a reload.
F11: 'not enabled' and 'Email not verified' refusals are retried three more times, adding rows and worker time for failures that waiting cannot fix.

na_reasons.F32: No promise of identical retry content and no stored rendered message: every retry re-runs the transport, so send-time content changes nothing in the design.
na_reasons.F39: Its footprint (Notification fields plus migration 0124, sendalerts and its tests, the log template, the webhook form, the changelog) already matches the precedents; the fact only speeds scoping and cannot change the design.

notes: F17 handled, with a defect: W2's revalidation ('Flip.select_channels() no longer includes the channel') reads the check's own channel_set, while Group.notify reaches members through group_channels (disabled ones included), so a failing member not assigned to the check is scheduled by W1 and then dropped by W2; group-routed deliveries would never be retried (P4 AD-15 covers this case).
F3 handled through the explicit retry_at state (AD-3 rejects deriving state from error text) and the decision not to retry unexpected exceptions; the 'Sending' marker itself is not named.
F12, F13 and F15 noted: quota counters, limit-notice emails and Signal CAPTCHA alerts firing once per attempt are 'accepted as inherent in S1' and left for the owner to confirm.
F14 handled only through the general non-permanent rule (rate-limited attempts are retried after at least a minute); the token buckets are not named.
F38 handled: W3 adds positive assertions for attempt rows; the vacuous existing test is not named.

worst_misses: F4: an over-200-character transport error fails the UPDATE that now also writes retry_at on PostgreSQL/MySQL, so the failure stays at 'Sending' and is never scheduled.
F27: AD-16 relies on the existing poll and W3 changes no JS, but the poll handler throws on the undefined dateFormat, so new attempt rows do not appear on an open page until a reload.

na_reasons.F32: No promise of identical retry content and no stored rendered message: every retry re-runs the transport, so send-time content changes nothing in the design.
na_reasons.F39: Its footprint (Notification fields plus migration 0124, sendalerts and its tests, the log template, the webhook form, the changelog) already matches the precedents; the fact only speeds scoping and cannot change the design.

notes: F13 and F15 handled by a new TransportError(retryable=False) at the SMS/WhatsApp/call monthly-limit refusals and SignalRateLimitFailure, with tests; F14 handled explicitly (rate-limit refusals retried on purpose).
F12 noted: one paid unit per attempt is accepted with no refund; retryable=False stops retries only once the monthly limit refuses.
F11 noted: 'not enabled' and 'Email not verified' refusals are retried and 'only add rows'.
F17 and F10: revalidation uses Flip.select_channels() plus the members of any group among its results, so members outside the check's channel list are still retried.
F37 handled for the code rules; CONTRIBUTING.md's AI policy is not mentioned.
F38 handled: W3 adds positive assertions for attempt rows; the vacuous existing test is not named.

worst_misses: F16: a pending down retry is sent even after the check recovered (Assumptions), so PagerDuty, PagerTree, Opsgenie, Splunk On-Call or a Pushover emergency alert re-opens an incident or restarts an alert that no recovery will close.

F12: each delayed retry of a failing SMS, WhatsApp or call delivery spends another paid unit (authorize_sms and authorize_call never refund), up to three per alert; the plan names only the limit refusals' emails.
F4: an over-200-character transport error fails the UPDATE that now also writes retry_at on PostgreSQL/MySQL, so such a failure stays at 'Sending' and is never retried.

na_reasons.F39: Its footprint (Notification fields plus migration 0124, sendalerts and its tests, the log template, the webhook form, the changelog) already matches the precedents; the fact only speeds scoping and cannot change the design.

notes: F10 handled for permanent errors, no-op (Channel.notify re-checks it) and deletion (CASCADE), but the plan deliberately sends retries to integrations disabled or unassigned after the failure (Assumptions).
F40 noted: the plan sends retries of superseded status changes and lists skipping them as the preferred, unrequested alternative.
F27 noted: the log.js defect is recorded as out of scope; attempts appear after a reload.
F11, F13 and F15 noted: 'not enabled' rows, repeated limit-notice emails and repeated Signal CAPTCHA mail are accepted, with a non-retryable flag left as the unrequested alternative.
F32 handled: the plan states that a retry is built at retry time ($JSON shows the check as it is now).
F14 handled only through the general non-permanent rule; the token buckets are not named.
F38 handled: W2 adds positive assertions for attempt rows; the vacuous existing test is not named.

verdict: P4 accounts for the most facts (34 handled, 3 missed, 2 noted): beyond the core all three share (one Notification row per attempt, a flip foreign key with a partial index, conditional-UPDATE claims inside sendalerts, group members retried individually, the corrected webhook sentence), it alone acts on the retry side effects (retryable=False for monthly-limit refusals, Signal CAPTCHA and the group row; rate-limit refusals retried on purpose) and revalidates group members outside the check's channel list, while P3 (32 handled, 4 missed, 3 noted) also drops retries superseded by a newer flip but only notes the quota, limit-notice and CAPTCHA repeats, misses the unfixable 'not enabled' refusals, and its select_channels revalidation would silently skip retries of group members not assigned to the check. P7 (31 handled, 4 missed, 5 noted) states its inherited decisions most explicitly and alone records the broken live-update script, but it knowingly sends retries after recovery and to disabled integrations, leaving the incident re-open hazard and the per-attempt SMS/call quota spend unaccounted; all three miss that an over-200-character transport error fails the UPDATE that now also schedules the retry.
